title: Omarchy Linux Gets a Foundation and Millions in Pledges
summary: Omarchy Linux funding explained: the Omacom Foundation, $18.5M in pledges, Hyprland sponsorship, Quickshell hiring, and new patron changes.
body_markdown:
The Omacom Foundation is the nonprofit DHH announced on 21 August 2026 to own the Omarchy trademarks and pay for the project around them: its infrastructure, its promotion, and the open-source work the distribution rests on.


The headline figure has moved since launch. The launch post is updated in place as new patrons join, the donor count keeps growing, and the foundation has started spending: three sponsorships, three full-time hires, and one sponsorship already replaced by a salary.


## Key Takeaways


- Omacom is the foundation and Omarchy is the Linux distribution; there is no entity called the Omarchy Foundation.
- DHH announced the Omacom Foundation on 21 August 2026 with eight Founding Patrons and $8 million in pledges. The launch post has been revised upward repeatedly since, and after DigitalOcean joined on 9 September 2026 it listed twelve Founding Patrons and approximately $18.5 million.
- Under a three-year deal with a two-year extension option, the foundation becomes Hyprland’s exclusive sponsor on 10 October, and the deal ends the paid Hyprperks subscriptions so the program opens up to everyone.
- On 9 September 2026 the foundation hired Quickshell creator outfoxxed as full-time Head of Omarchy Shell, replacing the three-year Quickshell sponsorship announced on 24 August.
- The foundation has said everything raised this year will be spent over 2027 to 2029, but no per-project dollar allocations have been published.


## What Is the Omacom Foundation?


Omacom is the name of the foundation; Omarchy is the name of the Linux distribution, and the phrase “Omarchy Foundation” that appears in some coverage refers to nothing that exists. In[the launch post](https://omarchy.org/news/2026/08/omacom-foundation-launches-with-8-million/) , DHH says he is setting it up as a nonprofit with four jobs: owning the trademarks, paying for infrastructure, promoting the work, and backing the open-source projects and developers that Omarchy is built on. The[foundation page](https://omarchy.org/foundation/) calls it the nonprofit funding the development, maintenance and spread of Omarchy. No official page states that incorporation is complete or names a jurisdiction.


The prompt for the fundraise, per the launch post, was the reception of Omarchy Quattro, the 4.0 release. Omarchy itself is assembled from three core technologies: Arch Linux, Hyprland, and Quickshell.


## How Much Has the Omacom Foundation Raised?


The foundation launched on 21 August 2026 with eight Founding Patrons and $8 million in pledges. The launch post is revised each time new money arrives, and after DigitalOcean joined on 9 September 2026 it listed twelve Founding Patrons and approximately $18.5 million in pledges and donations. The $8 million and eight-patron starting point is documented in[the 24 August update](https://omarchy.org/news/2026/08/omacom-foundation-funding-hits-10m/) , which added Drew Houston and Peter Steinberger to the original eight and took the total to $10 million.

Figures as the launch post listed them after its 9 September 2026 revision. New pledges and donations have arrived every few days since launch, so read the totals as a snapshot rather than a final tally. The running total counts multi-year corporate pledges at their full three-year value and token pledges at their stated dollar value, as set out in[the 3 September token announcement](https://omarchy.org/news/2026/09/omacom-foundation-secures-tokens-from-leading-labs/) and the 7 September update. That 9 September revision followed[DigitalOcean joining](https://omarchy.org/news/2026/09/digitalocean-joins-as-founding-corporate-patron/) with a $3 million three-year commitment.


## Hyprland: Exclusive Sponsorship of Vaxry From 10 October


Under a three-year agreement with a two-year extension option, the Omacom Foundation becomes the exclusive sponsor of Vaxry, the creator of Hyprland, on 10 October. The same deal ends the paid subscriptions to Hyprland’s Hyprperks program, so its contents open up to every user. Those terms come from[the Hyprland sponsorship post](https://omarchy.org/news/2026/08/omacom-foundation-to-be-exclusive-hyprland-sponsor/) published on 21 August 2026, the same day as the launch. The post states no dollar value for the deal and does not define what “exclusive” excludes; it does say Hyprland will keep accepting personal donations.


[Hyprperks](https://hypr.land/news/hyprperks/) is described on Hyprland’s own site as a paid subscription. The sponsorship post says the deal allows the program to go free, but it gives no date for that change. The post credits 37signals, Butterfly, and Framework as the sponsors who supported Hyprland before the handover.


## Why Did the Omacom Foundation Replace the Quickshell Sponsorship?


On 9 September 2026 the Omacom Foundation hired outfoxxed, the creator of Quickshell, as full-time Head of Omarchy Shell and a member of Omarchy Core, replacing the three-year Quickshell sponsorship it had announced on 24 August.[The hiring post](https://omarchy.org/news/2026/09/omacom-foundation-hires-outfoxxed/) describes Shell as everything you interact with on the desktop, from the bar and menus through to notifications and widgets, with Quickshell providing the QML pieces they are built from. It also puts the plugin catalogue at close to three thousand entries, up from the thousand-plus created in Quattro’s first week.


The superseded arrangement was[a “premier” Quickshell sponsorship](https://omarchy.org/news/2026/08/omacom-foundation-to-be-premier-quickshell-sponsor/) termed for three years, with no dollar value published; that post now carries a 9 September note recording the change. The 9 September post calls outfoxxed the foundation’s second full-time hire, after[Krzysztof Wilczyński](https://omarchy.org/news/2026/09/omacom-foundation-hires-krzysztof-wilczynski/) , announced 3 September 2026 as Head of Omarchy Kernel. A third,[Emir Beganović as Head of Infrastructure](https://omarchy.org/news/2026/09/omacom-foundation-hires-emir-beganovic/) , was announced on 10 September and starts 1 November. The foundation says hiring will remain selective and based on community contribution rather than open applications.


## What Changes for Developers Outside Omarchy?


Two of the three core technologies in Omarchy now have their creators on funded time, and one of them has a paid tier scheduled to disappear. For anyone running Hyprland on a different distribution, the 21 August 2026 announcement says the sponsorship lets Hyprperks go free, with personal donations still accepted; the date published is for the sponsorship itself, which starts on 10 October. For anyone building on Quickshell, its creator is employed full time by the Omacom Foundation, with the 9 September post naming performance, reliability, plugin authoring, and security as the areas of work.


The third sponsorship reaches further outside Omarchy again. On 25 August 2026 the foundation became a[premier sponsor of mise](https://omarchy.org/news/2026/08/omacom-foundation-to-be-premier-mise-sponsor/) and of its creator jdx. mise handles language runtimes, and it wraps Omarchy’s coding-agent CLIs as stubs that install themselves the first time you run one. No dollar figure was published for this deal either.


Allocation intent for the remainder is stated in[the 3 September spending post](https://omarchy.org/news/2026/09/omacom-foundation-accelerates-spending-goals/) : this year’s money is to go out across 2027, 2028 and 2029 rather than sit in an endowment, which on the $13 million committed at that point meant yearly budgets of more than $4 million. The post lists where it should land: the upstream open-source projects Omarchy is built on, the artists who make it look the way it does, the developers who maintain it, and then competitions, grants and infrastructure.


## What the Announcements Do Not Say


None of the posts publishes a dollar value for the Hyprland sponsorship, the mise sponsorship, the superseded Quickshell sponsorship, or any of the three salaries. The 3 September spending post lists categories but no per-category amounts, and no official page describes a board, a governance structure, or the legal jurisdiction of incorporation. The gap between the total pledged and the commitments disclosed so far is where the next set of announcements will land.


The omarchy.org news feed holds the record: the launch post carries the running total, and the individual sponsorship and hiring posts show what that total has funded. If you depend on Hyprland or Quickshell, 10 October is when the Hyprland deal begins, and the sponsorships page is where the next funded project will appear.


## FAQs


Is Hyprperks free now that the Omacom Foundation is sponsoring Hyprland?


Not yet, and no date has been published for the change. The Omacom Foundation's sponsorship of Vaxry begins on 10 October, and the 21 August 2026 sponsorship post says the deal allows Hyprperks to go free for everyone as the paid subscriptions end, without giving a separate date for it. Hyprland's own announcement, dated 28 July 2025, describes Hyprperks as a subscription costing 5 euros plus tax a month, covering access to a members' forum and a ready-made set of dotfiles.


What does 'tokens' mean in the Omacom Foundation's pledge totals?


Tokens are AI model usage donated by the labs for the coding agents that build Omarchy, not cryptocurrency. The 3 September 2026 post says Omarchy Quattro was built almost entirely by agents, and the foundation counts token pledges at their stated dollar value: $1.5 million from Meta Superintelligence Labs and $150,000 each from Anthropic, OpenAI and Fireworks, with OpenRouter pledging the same amount on 7 September.


Does the Omacom Foundation sponsor anything besides Hyprland and Quickshell?


Yes. On 25 August 2026 the Omacom Foundation announced a 'premier' sponsorship of mise and its creator jdx, its third sponsorship after Hyprland and Quickshell. mise looks after language runtimes in Omarchy, and the major coding-agent CLIs ship as mise stubs that only install themselves the first time you run them. The post publishes no dollar figure, and mise is not one of Omarchy's three core technologies.


How can individual developers donate to the Omacom Foundation?


Through the open patronage program at donate.omarchy.org, which accepts any amount and lists donors on the patrons page by tier: 16B for $16 or more, 256B for $256 or more, 2K for $2,048 or more, and 8K for $8,192 or more, each with a badge to collect. As of its 9 September 2026 revision, the launch post reported nearly 500 donors contributing roughly $60,000 this way, and the patrons page adds names as more people join. Prospective Founding or Distinguished Patrons are directed to contact DHH by email.
